title: An array literal's own type is synthesized for one code action, and no compile path asks for it
scope:
the *narrow this annotation to the literal's type* code action — what it reads, what it
writes, when it declines to answer, where its one new function lives, and why it never runs on save.
It does **not** decide the object-shape rewrite a record-shaped literal really wants
([0036](0036.md) owns shapes, and this action never changes a value's kind), it
adds **no diagnostic and no hint** — nothing here makes the checker say anything it does not already
say — and it does not cover narrowing from writes made *after* the declaration, which *Revisiting*
holds. M4B's frozen set is untouched: [0099](0099.md) draws
that boundary and this decision sits on the far side of it.
dependsOnText: [0007](0007.md) — § 5 is the container this decides how to spell.

summary.headline: The editor can narrow `array<mixed>` to the type a literal actually holds
summary.body:
Writing `array<array<array<float>>>` by hand is tedious, so a nested literal often gets
annotated `array<mixed>` and loses type checking for good. The editor offers a fix: on an array
literal right there in the source, it works out the narrowest type covering every element and
proposes the spelling you could have typed. It answers only from the literal itself, declines
when the value comes from input or would still be `mixed`, and always presents a diff to
approve, never a silent change on save. The compiler never uses this; the language is unchanged.
